annotations.description: Playing basic Island instead of Watery Grave on turn 1 is slightly suboptimal. The hand contains Essence Scatter (1U), Negate (1U), and Requiting Hex (B). Playing Watery Grave (paying 2 life) would give access to both U and B on turn 2 with any second land, enabling both countermagic and Requiting Hex. Playing Island first means if they draw no other blue source, they need to sequence Watery Grave later anyway. More importantly, with Watery Grave turn 1, they can play Island turn 2 and have UU+B available, or play Swamp turn 2 and have UB available. With Island turn 1, playing Swamp turn 2 gives only UB (can cast Requiting Hex or Negate but not Essence Scatter which needs 1U), while Watery Grave turn 2 untapped costs life anyway. The key consideration is that playing Watery Grave now preserves flexibility and the 2 life cost is the same whether paid now or later. Playing Island first is defensible since it avoids the life payment, but with a hand full of reactive spells wanting early mana flexibility, Watery Grave untapped turn 1 is generally better.

annotations.betterLine: Play Watery Grave paying 2 life to have access to both U and B mana immediately, maximizing flexibility for reactive spells in hand

Playing Hushwood Verge first, then Breeding Pool Turn 2 (paying 2 life) provides G+GU, enabling the powerful Doc Aurlock on curve.

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Watery Grave (paying 2 life) is suboptimal here. With Island + Swamp, GPT4om has access to UB but cannot cast Negate (which costs 1U - needs two sources including U). With Watery Grave (untapped), they'd have Island + Watery Grave giving them access to UU or UB, enabling both Essence Scatter and Negate on turn 2. Playing Swamp means they can only hold up one of their two-mana counterspells (Essence Scatter with Island+Swamp for 1U works, but Negate also works with 1U). Actually, both Island + Swamp = U + B, which gives 1U for either Essence Scatter or Negate. So the mana works the same for counterspells this turn. However, Watery Grave would be better played now while the opponent has limited pressure, preserving Swamp for a later turn when life total matters more. More importantly, playing Watery Grave now keeps Restless Reef available for later (it enters tapped), and Watery Grave provides more flexible mana (both U and B from one land). The difference is marginal since both lines leave up 1U for counters, but Watery Grave is slightly better for future flexibility.

annotations.betterLine: Play Watery Grave paying 2 life to have more flexible mana (U/B dual) while opponent's board is still undeveloped, saving the basic Swamp for later when life total may matter more

annotations.description: Playing Doc Aurlock before playing the land from hand is a sequencing error. The player has Hallowed Fountain and Starting Town in hand. They should play a land first (Starting Town enters untapped on turn 2, or Hallowed Fountain paying 2 life) to have more mana available, or at minimum to not miss the land drop if something unexpected happens. More importantly, casting Doc Aurlock into open mana (the opponent has Island + Swamp, exactly enough for Essence Scatter) is risky. While this can't always be avoided with a 2-drop, the player could have played the land first and then cast Badgermole Cub instead, which would earthbend a land and provide mana acceleration - arguably a stronger turn 2 play that also doesn't lose to the legend rule since they have two Doc Aurlocks. However, Doc Aurlock is a reasonable turn 2 play for its cost reduction abilities. The main concrete error is not playing the land before casting the creature.

annotations.betterLine: Play Starting Town (or Hallowed Fountain) first, then cast the creature. Could also consider casting Badgermole Cub instead to get earthbend value and mana acceleration, since holding two copies of legendary Doc Aurlock means the second copy is dead weight.

annotations.description: With 3 lands available (Breeding Pool for G/U, Hushwood Verge for G/W, Hallowed Fountain for W/U), the player could cast Doc Aurlock (GU) or Badgermole Cub (1G) or Airbender Ascension (1W) instead of Llanowar Elves. The opponent has 3 lands with only 2 untapped (Island and Swamp), meaning they likely have Essence Scatter/counter mana available. Playing Llanowar Elves into potential counter mana is less punishing than losing a 2-drop like Doc Aurlock, but the opponent already used Essence Scatter on a previous Doc Aurlock (it's in both graveyards). Playing Llanowar Elves first is a reasonable 'test the waters' play, but the player could have led with Airbender Ascension (a noncreature spell that dodges Essence Scatter) to get value and then followed up with Llanowar Elves. With 1W available after tapping for Airbender Ascension (tap Hushwood Verge for W, Hallowed Fountain for W... no, need 1W = 2 mana). Actually: tap Breeding Pool for G, Hallowed Fountain for W = cast Airbender Ascension for 1W? No, 1W needs one generic + one white. Tap Breeding Pool (G) + Hallowed Fountain (W) = GW, which pays 1W. Then Hushwood Verge is untapped but only produces G (no Forest/Plains in type... wait, Breeding Pool is Forest Island, so Hushwood Verge can tap for W or G). So after casting Airbender Ascension, Hushwood Verge could tap for G to cast Llanowar Elves. This line gets both Airbender Ascension (dodges creature counters) AND Llanowar Elves on the same turn, which is strictly better than just Llanowar Elves alone.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Airbender Ascension first (tap Breeding Pool for G + Hallowed Fountain for W = 1W), then cast Llanowar Elves (tap Hushwood Verge for G), deploying two permanents this turn instead of one. Airbender Ascension dodges Essence Scatter since it's a noncreature spell.

annotations.description: GPT4om Libby used Requiting Hex to destroy Starting Town (a 1/1 animated land) instead of Llanowar Elves (a 1/1 mana dork). Starting Town is an earthbent land - when it dies, it returns to the battlefield tapped as a regular land, so destroying it doesn't actually remove any permanent from the board. The opponent loses the 1/1 body but gets the land back. Destroying Llanowar Elves would permanently remove a mana dork, denying the opponent mana acceleration. Alternatively, Badgermole Cub (mana value 2) is also a valid target and would be a permanent removal of a 2/2 creature body. Given that Libby is at 7 life and needs to reduce the opponent's board pressure, killing the Badgermole Cub (removing a real 2/2 threat permanently) or at minimum the Llanowar Elves (removing mana acceleration permanently) would have been better than killing an animated land that just comes back.

annotations.description: Deadly Cover-Up with evidence collected lets you exile a card from the opponent's graveyard and then search their graveyard, hand, and library for all copies to exile them. Choosing Hallowed Fountain - a land - is nearly worthless since the opponent has no more copies in hand or library that matter strategically. The opponent's graveyard contains key threats like Badgermole Cub (2 copies), Doc Aurlock, Grizzled Genius (2 copies), and Llanowar Elves (2 copies). Exiling Badgermole Cub or Doc Aurlock would strip additional copies from the opponent's hand and library, significantly weakening their future game plan. At 1 life, GPT4om Libby desperately needs to prevent the opponent from rebuilding, and removing a key creature from all zones would be far more impactful than exiling a land.
